Practical AI Adoption in Sub-Saharan Africa: Procurement, Local Adaptation and the Productivity Opportunity

Artificial intelligence is reaching African workers, firms and public institutions before the foundations for dependable use are evenly in place. The immediate opportunity is not to reproduce a frontier-model race. It is to procure and adapt task-specific tools that work with local languages, trusted data, affordable access and accountable institutions. This paper examines how Sub-Saharan African governments and investors can turn early adoption into productivity while keeping implementation risk visible.
